action: Escalate the public-S3 -> IMDSv1 -> IAM-wildcard exposure chain: hand off to cloud-workload-protection for runtime containment and identity-access-risk for the over-permissive role.
rationale: CSPM scan of AWS account 123456789012 (us-east-1, us-west-2) against CIS AWS Foundations 1.5. 5 findings across 22 checks; 4 form a single exploitable chain: a public-read S3 bucket holding customer exports (CIS 2.1.5), an internet-facing EC2 still permitting IMDSv1 (CIS 5.6), an app-runtime IAM role with Action:*/Resource:* (CIS 1.16), and CloudTrail disabled in us-west-2 (CIS 3.1) masking the path. Internet-facing + production + regulated-data modifiers upgrade the chain to high. Confidence 0.86: 3 agreeing sources (Security Hub finding, config snapshot, IAM policy read); best tier secondary, corroboration lift (per standards/confidence-rubric.md).
key_findings: CSP-001 public-s3-bucket - arn:aws:s3:::acme-prod-customer-exports has a public-read ACL (CIS AWS 2.1.5); bucket holds customer PII exports
CSP-002 imdsv1-enabled - instance i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8 (internet-facing) permits IMDSv1 with HttpTokens=optional (CIS AWS 5.6); SSRF -> instance-credential theft path
CSP-003 iam-wildcard - role/app-runtime policy allows Action:* on Resource:* (CIS AWS 1.16); enables lateral movement once instance credentials are stolen
CSP-004 cloudtrail-disabled - CloudTrail is off in us-west-2 (CIS AWS 3.1); masks the S3 read and API activity in the exfiltration path
CSP-005 rds-unencrypted - db-prod-billing lacks encryption at rest (CIS AWS 2.3.1); medium severity, outside the primary chain
